findings.title: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938): Frequently asked questions about OpenJDK remote code execution vulnerability
findings.summary: Java4Shell is a flaw in how Java decodes Base64 data. Calif, which found it, says it can let attackers run code on widely used Java applications without logging in. Oracle released fixed Java builds on November 17, and Calif is withholding its exploits for individual applications for now. Change log Update November 18: Added reports of exploitation attempts and a working exploit, alerts from CISA and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, fixed builds from other Java distributions, mitigation guidance from Keycloak and an example Tenable Hexa AI prompt. Click here to review the change log history Update November 18: Added reports of exploitation attempts and a working exploit, alerts from CISA and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, fixed builds from other Java distributions, mitigation guidance from Keycloak and an example Tenable Hexa AI prompt. November 17: Original publication. Key takeaways CVE-2026-114938, dubbed Java4Shell, is an OpenJDK memory corruption vulnerability that Oracle scores 8.1 on CVSS 3.1, and Calif says its testing showed attackers could run code without logging in on applications such as Atlassian Jira and Jenkins. As of November 18, GreyNoise has reported exploitation attempts against this flaw but has not confirmed any successful exploitation against its sensors, and VulnCheck says a working exploit is available to its customers, while Kevin Breen of Immersive reports building one. Oracle released fixed builds on November 17, and according to Calif, only systems running an affected Java version on x86-64 processors that support AVX-512 VBMI can be affected. findings.title: Vulnerabilities in Node.js and Brotli Affecting Cisco Products: October 2026
findings.summary: On October 21, 2026, Node.js announced the availability of fixes for multiple vulnerabilities across the following supported release lines: 22.x, 24.x, and 26.x. These vulnerabilities impact critical operations such as the Brotli decoder, DNS resolution, and TLS certificate validation. The vulnerabilities pose risks for remote code execution and traffic interception. For more information, see Node.js Security Release . The following vulnerabilities have a Security Impact Rating (SIR) of High and are addressed in this advisory: CVE-2026-111497 - Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write; potential remote code execution CVE-2026-105482 - DNS resolution truncation involving embedded NUL characters CVE-2026-105483 - TLS hostname validation bypass using fullwidth IP digits CVE-2026-106069 - TLS hostname validation bypass with noncanonical IP addresses For information about Splunk products and offerings, including AppDynamics, see Vulnerabilities in Node.js (CVE-2026-111497, CVE-2026-105482, CVE-2026-105483, CVE-2026-106069) on Splunk Products - October 2026 This investigation was expanded to cover Brotli outside of Node.js on October 30, 2026. The Brotli decoder flaw (CVE-2026-111497), which is in the Google Brotli C decoder, is often bundled with or linked to other software, so products beyond Node.js may be affected. For software that may be affected, see Broccoli2Shell . Important: If a product is not listed within this advisory, Cisco's review indicates that the product is not affected by this vulnerability. This advisory will be updated as additional information becomes available. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-oct2026-node-js-Jj3SQ19u Security Impact Rating: High CVE: CVE-2026-105482,CVE-2026-105483,CVE-2026-106069,CVE-2026-111497

findings.title: CVE-2024-10441 — Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output Vulnerability
findings.summary: Vendor: Synology | Product: DiskStation Manager (DSM). Synology DSM contains an improper encoding or escaping of output vulnerability in the system plugin daemon in Synology BeeStation OS (BSM) that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via unspecified vectors. Required action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines. (due 2026-11-21)

findings.title: CVE-2026-90817 — Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) Code Injection Vulnerability
findings.summary: Vendor: Vanderbilt University | Product: Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap). Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) contains a code injection vulnerability which could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server. An attacker could exploit this via crafted HTTP requests that access an unintended controller route from a public survey context and supply a crafted file-path or stream parameter during data import processing. Exploitation requires knowledge of a valid public survey hash. Required action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines. (due 2026-11-21)

findings.title: CVE-2026-90436 — Apache Axis Unsafe Reflection Vulnerability
findings.summary: Vendor: Apache | Product: Axis. Apache Axis contains an unsafe reflection vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via a crafted SOAP fault message that causes Axis to load and instantiate an attacker-specified class when a suitable class is available on the application classpath. The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users are advised to discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version. Required action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines. (due 2026-11-21)
